units.translation: it would become long if I wanted to enumerate from the beginning with whom I have been together without infecting him. Since Musgrave, line 286 has been deleted, not as not originating from the poet, but as added from elsewhere for explanation. If, however, one writes ⟦1⟧ and not (manuscript) ⟦2⟧, then it is by no means foreign to the context, cf. above (Paley). ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧, ⟦5⟧ ⟦6⟧. ⟦7⟧ like ⟦8⟧ (⟦9⟧ ⟦10⟧).
at the same time growing old
time as it grows old teaches all things
there is no old age for this pollution
⟦1⟧ also at 299, 614; ⟦2⟧ (on 235) likewise three times, and besides ⟦3⟧.

⟦1⟧ is also found in the inscriptions of this period (alongside ⟦2⟧), Meisterhans-Schwyzer 31, 157. — 289 f.: cf. 762 ff. the fulfillment of this promise (see also 671 ff. Apollo). The suppliant seeks to draw the god into his interest, see on ⟦3⟧

292 ff. The general form of invocation of a god is that of the various places where he may reside, where he enjoys worship; thus the more numerous and the more distant the places, the greater his power. So already Glaucus in Homer Π 514: ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧· ⟦3⟧. Orestes now names two peculiarly chosen places: the Tritonian lake in Libya and the Phlegraean fields in Pallene. The lake had become known to the Greeks through the Cyrenaeans, which is why Pindar also mentions it in Pythian IV, 20; the neighboring Libyans, ⟦4⟧ according to ⟦5⟧, worshipped a warlike goddess, whom the Hellenes immediately identified with their Athena and knew how to reconcile the Libyan mythology, according to which she was a daughter of Poseidon and ⟦6⟧, with their own; Athena had given herself to Zeus out of anger she had felt toward her father. Herodotus does not speak at all of a river ⟦7⟧; according to others, such as ⟦8⟧, this was the name of the outflow of the lake situated near the coast. But also in Hellas there were several rivers of that name, and everywhere the legend of the birth of Athena was attached to them, in accordance with the ancient epithet ⟦9⟧ (Homer Δ 515 etc.), which undoubtedly means the one born from the water (⟦10⟧, ⟦11⟧), Preller-Robert Myth. 186 f. Since, however, the opinions of scholars differed about the origin of the name (Schol. Δ 515 ⟦12⟧), the scholiast here remarks: ⟦13⟧. Whether and how Aeschylus combined this conception with that of the birth from the head of Zeus (see line 736) remains unclear.
